scr_budgeting_job_positions_list.purpose: Lists the site job positions used for payroll budgeting — community manager, assistant manager, leasing consultant, maintenance supervisor, maintenance technician, porter — with their default pay, hours and workers' comp class.
scr_budgeting_job_positions_list.outcome: A standard position catalog so payroll is budgeted consistently across properties.
scr_budgeting_job_positions_list.rootCause: Payroll budgets are built position by position. A shared catalog with default pay and class ensures, for example, that every maintenance technician is budgeted with the maintenance workers' comp class and a market-based wage.
scr_budgeting_job_positions_list.ifSkipped: Each property invents its own positions and pay assumptions, and payroll budgets cannot be compared across the portfolio.
redFlags: Positions without a workers' comp class

scr_budgeting_adding_a_job_position.purpose: Adds a new job position to the payroll planning catalog with its default wage, hours, overtime assumption and workers' comp class — for example a new 'Resident Experience Coordinator' role.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_job_position.outcome: New roles can be budgeted with consistent default assumptions.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_job_position.rootCause: Operating models change (centralized leasing, new amenity staff); new roles need catalog entries before properties can budget them, or they get forced into ill-fitting positions with wrong rates.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_job_position.ifSkipped: New roles are budgeted under unrelated positions with wrong wages and burden.
redFlags: Positions created without default wage assumptions

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_job_po.purpose: Views or updates a job position's defaults — typically raising default wages for market adjustments before the budget cycle.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_job_po.outcome: Position defaults reflect current market wages and policies.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_job_po.rootCause: Wage markets move quickly for leasing and maintenance roles; outdated defaults produce payroll budgets that are too low and variances all year.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_job_po.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets understate wages and show unfavorable variances from January.
redFlags: Default wages unchanged for multiple years

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_job_position.purpose: Deletes a job position no longer used in the operating model, such as a role eliminated by centralizing leasing.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_job_position.outcome: The catalog contains only current roles.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_job_position.rootCause: Obsolete positions remain selectable and can be budgeted by mistake, adding payroll for roles the property no longer staffs.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_job_position.ifSkipped: Budgets include payroll for eliminated roles, overstating expenses.
redFlags: Deleting positions still assigned to employees

scr_budgeting_new_job_position_page.purpose: The page for adding, viewing or editing a job position's details — title, wage basis (hourly or salary), default rate, hours and workers' comp class.
scr_budgeting_new_job_position_page.outcome: Complete position definitions for payroll calculation.
scr_budgeting_new_job_position_page.rootCause: Each field drives the payroll calculation; a salaried position set as hourly with 40 hours plus overtime produces a wrong budget.
scr_budgeting_new_job_position_page.ifSkipped: Payroll calculations use incomplete or wrong position data.
redFlags: Non-exempt roles budgeted without overtime

scr_budgeting_employees_list.purpose: Lists employee records used in payroll planning — typically synchronized from the payroll system — with position, property, wage and status.
scr_budgeting_employees_list.outcome: Payroll budgets built from actual staff and wages rather than generic positions.
scr_budgeting_employees_list.rootCause: Budgeting from the real employee roster (current wages, open positions) is far more accurate than escalating last year's payroll total.
scr_budgeting_employees_list.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets ignore current wages and vacancies.
redFlags: Terminated employees still in the planning roster

scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_record.purpose: Adds an employee record manually in payroll planning — normally unnecessary because employees come from the payroll interface, but used for planned new hires.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_record.outcome: Planned hires can be budgeted by name or as open positions.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_record.rootCause: Budgets must include positions the property plans to fill; adding them explicitly avoids understating payroll.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_record.ifSkipped: Planned hires are left out and payroll is understated.
redFlags: Manual employees duplicating interfaced records

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.purpose: Views or updates an employee's planning data — wage, position, allocation across properties, planned raises.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.rootCause: Raises, promotions and shared-staff allocations change payroll cost by property; employee-level edits capture them.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_employ.ifSkipped: Raises and allocations are missing from the budget.
redFlags: Shared staff allocated over 100% across properties

scr_budgeting_deleting_an_employee_recor.purpose: Deletes an employee record from payroll planning, for example a duplicate or an employee who left before the budget year.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_employee_recor.outcome: The planning roster reflects actual staffing.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_employee_recor.rootCause: Departed employees left in the roster are budgeted at their old wage, overstating payroll.
scr_budgeting_deleting_an_employee_recor.ifSkipped: Payroll includes employees who no longer work at the property.
redFlags: Positions deleted without planning a replacement

scr_budgeting_employee_page.purpose: The employee record page for payroll planning — name, position, property, wage, hours and allocations.
scr_budgeting_employee_page.outcome: A complete employee definition for payroll calculation.
scr_budgeting_employee_page.rootCause: Allocations across properties matter: shared maintenance staff must be charged to each property in the right proportion.
scr_budgeting_employee_page.ifSkipped: Shared staff costs land at one property instead of being allocated.
redFlags: Missing allocations for shared staff

scr_budgeting_federal_taxes_list.purpose: Lists federal payroll tax settings for budgeting — Social Security and Medicare (FICA) rates and wage bases, and FUTA rate and wage base — by year.
scr_budgeting_federal_taxes_list.outcome: Payroll burden budgets use the correct federal rates and caps.
scr_budgeting_federal_taxes_list.rootCause: Federal payroll taxes are a fixed-percentage burden with annual wage bases (the Social Security wage base changes every year). Using wrong caps misstates burden for higher-paid staff.
scr_budgeting_federal_taxes_list.ifSkipped: Payroll tax budgets are misstated, especially for managers above the FUTA or FICA wage bases.
redFlags: Prior-year Social Security wage base used

scr_budgeting_adding_federal_taxes.purpose: Sets up the federal payroll tax parameters for a new budget year — Social Security and Medicare rates, the Social Security wage base, and the FUTA rate and wage base — used in every payroll calculation.
scr_budgeting_adding_federal_taxes.outcome: The new budget year has correct federal tax parameters.
scr_budgeting_adding_federal_taxes.rootCause: Wage bases change annually; each budget year needs its own settings or the calculation carries last year's figures.
scr_budgeting_adding_federal_taxes.ifSkipped: Budgets use outdated federal tax parameters.
redFlags: Missing settings for the budget year

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_federa.purpose: Views or updates federal payroll tax settings when rates or wage bases are announced for the new year.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_federa.rootCause: The SSA announces the new wage base each autumn, often after budgeting starts; settings must be updated when it is published.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_federa.ifSkipped: Budgets finalize on estimated rather than published wage bases.
redFlags: Edits after payroll budgets were published without recalculation

scr_budgeting_deleting_federal_taxes.purpose: Deletes a set of federal payroll tax settings that was entered in error, such as a duplicate record for the same budget year.
scr_budgeting_deleting_federal_taxes.outcome: Only one valid set of federal settings per year remains.
scr_budgeting_deleting_federal_taxes.rootCause: Two sets of federal settings for the same year make it unclear which rates a payroll calculation used, and the wrong set may be applied to every property's payroll budget.
scr_budgeting_deleting_federal_taxes.ifSkipped: Payroll calculations may pick the wrong set of rates.
redFlags: Deleting the only settings for an active budget year

scr_budgeting_federal_tax_page.purpose: The page where federal payroll tax rates (FICA and FUTA percentages) and their annual wage bases are entered for a budget year and applied to every employee's payroll calculation.
scr_budgeting_federal_tax_page.rootCause: Rates and caps entered here apply to every employee's budget; one error distorts payroll burden across the portfolio.
scr_budgeting_federal_tax_page.ifSkipped: Federal burden errors spread to every property.
redFlags: Rates entered as whole numbers instead of percentages

scr_budgeting_state_taxes_list.purpose: Lists state payroll tax settings — state unemployment (SUTA) rates and wage bases, and other state-specific payroll taxes — by state and year.
scr_budgeting_state_taxes_list.outcome: Payroll burden reflects each state's rates and wage bases.
scr_budgeting_state_taxes_list.rootCause: SUTA rates vary by state and by employer experience; wage bases range widely. Portfolios across several states need state-specific settings for accurate burden.
scr_budgeting_state_taxes_list.ifSkipped: State payroll taxes are budgeted with one generic rate, misstating burden.
redFlags: States in the portfolio without settings

scr_budgeting_adding_a_state_tax.purpose: Adds a state's payroll tax settings for a budget year — the employer's SUTA rate, the state wage base and any other state payroll taxes — so properties in that state budget burden correctly.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_state_tax.outcome: Properties in that state budget payroll taxes correctly.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_state_tax.rootCause: Entering a new state (acquisition) requires its payroll tax settings before payroll can be budgeted there.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_state_tax.ifSkipped: New-state properties are budgeted without state taxes.
redFlags: Employer-specific SUTA rate not used

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_state_.purpose: Views or updates state payroll tax settings when the state issues the employer's new SUTA rate notice.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_state_.outcome: State burden uses the current employer rate.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_state_.rootCause: Employer SUTA rates change annually with claims experience; stale rates misstate burden.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_state_.ifSkipped: State payroll burden is budgeted on last year's employer rate and misstated for every property in that state.
redFlags: Rates not updated after state notice

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_state_tax.purpose: Deletes state payroll tax settings that were entered in error or are no longer needed after exiting a state.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_state_tax.outcome: State tax settings reflect current operations.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_state_tax.rootCause: Duplicate or obsolete state tax settings can be picked up by payroll calculations for the wrong properties, applying another state's rates and wage base to their payroll budgets.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_state_tax.ifSkipped: Wrong state rates applied to payroll budgets.
redFlags: Deleting settings still used by active properties

scr_budgeting_state_tax_page.purpose: The page where a state's payroll tax rates and wage base are entered for a budget year, applied to every employee budgeted at properties in that state.
scr_budgeting_state_tax_page.rootCause: State parameters apply to every employee budgeted in that state; errors multiply across properties.
scr_budgeting_state_tax_page.ifSkipped: State burden errors spread across the state's properties.
redFlags: Wage base missing

scr_budgeting_benefits_list.purpose: Lists employee benefits used in payroll planning — medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance — with employer costs by year and plan.
scr_budgeting_benefits_list.outcome: Benefit costs budgeted per employee based on actual plans.
scr_budgeting_benefits_list.rootCause: Benefits can add 20-30% to wages and vary by plan and coverage tier. Budgeting them from plan costs rather than a flat percentage improves accuracy.
scr_budgeting_benefits_list.ifSkipped: Benefit budgets are rough percentages and miss renewal increases.
redFlags: Benefit costs not updated for the plan renewal

scr_budgeting_adding_a_benefit.purpose: Adds a benefit plan with its employer cost for a year — useful when the company offers many plans across regions.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_benefit.outcome: New plans available for employee budget assignments.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_benefit.rootCause: Plan changes at renewal (new carriers, tiers) require new benefit records so employees are budgeted at correct costs.
scr_budgeting_adding_a_benefit.ifSkipped: Employees are budgeted on outdated plans.
redFlags: Plans added without employer cost

scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_benefi.purpose: Views or updates a benefit plan's employer cost by coverage level after the annual renewal, so payroll budgets reflect renewal pricing.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_benefi.rootCause: Medical renewals often increase 5-10% or more; updating costs prevents understated benefits.
scr_budgeting_viewing_and_editing_benefi.ifSkipped: Benefits are budgeted at last year's cost and show unfavorable variances all year.
redFlags: Costs unchanged from prior year

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_benefit.purpose: Deletes a benefit plan that is no longer offered, such as a carrier dropped at renewal.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_benefit.outcome: Only benefit plans actually offered remain assignable in payroll budgets.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_benefit.rootCause: Discontinued plans left in the list are assigned by mistake and budget at old costs.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_benefit.ifSkipped: Employees are budgeted on discontinued plans.
redFlags: Deleting plans still assigned to employees

scr_budgeting_benefit_page.purpose: The page to add, view or edit a benefit plan's employer cost by year and coverage level.
scr_budgeting_benefit_page.rootCause: Coverage-level costs (employee only vs family) differ greatly; entering them correctly determines benefit budget accuracy.
scr_budgeting_benefit_page.ifSkipped: Benefit budgets ignore coverage levels and understate family-coverage costs.
redFlags: Single cost used for all coverage levels

scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench.purpose: The payroll workbench where payroll budgets are created, calculated from positions, employees, taxes and benefits, and published to working budgets.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench.outcome: A calculated payroll budget by property ready to publish.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench.rootCause: Payroll calculation combines many inputs; the workbench is where they come together and are reviewed before feeding the operating budget.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench.ifSkipped: Payroll is budgeted outside the system with less rigor.
redFlags: Payroll not refreshed after rate changes

scr_budgeting_payroll_list.purpose: Lists payroll budgets by property and year with status, calculation date and publish status.
scr_budgeting_payroll_list.outcome: Visibility of which properties' payroll budgets are calculated and published.
scr_budgeting_payroll_list.rootCause: Payroll budgets must be calculated and published for every property before the operating budget is final.
scr_budgeting_payroll_list.ifSkipped: Some properties' payroll is never published and the operating budget omits payroll.
redFlags: Properties with no published payroll

scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.purpose: Creates a payroll budget for a property and year and calculates wages, overtime, taxes, benefits and workers' comp from the setup tables.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.outcome: A detailed payroll budget calculated from current assumptions.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.rootCause: Calculating from components produces a payroll budget that can be explained line by line to the asset manager.
scr_budgeting_adding_and_calculating_a_p.ifSkipped: Payroll is estimated as a lump sum that cannot be explained.
redFlags: Calculation run before tax and benefit tables were updated

scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.purpose: Publishes a calculated payroll budget into a working budget, populating the payroll, tax and benefit accounts.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.outcome: Payroll lines in the operating budget come from the detailed calculation.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.rootCause: Publishing links the payroll model to the operating budget so changes in staffing assumptions flow through consistently.
scr_budgeting_publishing_a_payroll_to_a_.ifSkipped: Operating budget payroll lines differ from the payroll model.
redFlags: Publishing to the wrong working budget

scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.purpose: Shows when a property's payroll budget was published, by whom and into which working budget, to trace the origin of payroll lines in the operating budget.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.outcome: Traceability of payroll figures in the operating budget.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.rootCause: When payroll lines in the budget change unexpectedly, publish history shows whether payroll was republished.
scr_budgeting_viewing_the_publish_histor.ifSkipped: Changes to payroll lines in the operating budget cannot be traced back to a publish event.
redFlags: Republishing after approval

scr_budgeting_refreshing_a_payrolls_calc.purpose: Recalculates a payroll budget after changes to positions, employees, taxes or benefits.
scr_budgeting_refreshing_a_payrolls_calc.outcome: Payroll budgets reflect the latest assumptions.
scr_budgeting_refreshing_a_payrolls_calc.rootCause: Rate updates (new wage base, benefit renewal) arrive during budget season; payrolls calculated before them must be refreshed.
redFlags: Refresh not followed by republishing

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_payroll.purpose: Deletes a payroll budget that was created in error or has been superseded by a recalculated version for the same property and year.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_payroll.outcome: Only the valid payroll budget remains for each property and year.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_payroll.rootCause: Duplicate payroll budgets can be published in error, doubling or replacing payroll lines in the operating budget.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_payroll.ifSkipped: Duplicate payroll budgets exist and the wrong one may be published into the operating budget.
redFlags: Deleting the published payroll

scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench_page.purpose: The payroll workbench page for creating, calculating, refreshing, publishing and reviewing payroll budgets.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench_page.outcome: One place to manage payroll budgeting for all properties.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench_page.rootCause: Payroll budgeting across many properties needs a central page to track status and act in bulk during budget season.
scr_budgeting_payroll_workbench_page.ifSkipped: Payroll budgets are tracked in side lists.
redFlags: Properties without calculated payroll

scr_budgeting_employees_of_entity_name_l.purpose: Lists employees included in a property's payroll budget, with positions, wages and allocations.
scr_budgeting_employees_of_entity_name_l.outcome: Visibility of exactly whose payroll makes up the property budget.
scr_budgeting_employees_of_entity_name_l.rootCause: Reviewers verify payroll budgets by checking the headcount and wages behind them; the list shows that directly.
scr_budgeting_employees_of_entity_name_l.ifSkipped: Headcount errors (missing or extra staff) go unnoticed.
redFlags: Headcount different from the approved staffing plan

scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_the_.purpose: Adds an employee or a planned open position to a property's payroll budget — for example a second leasing consultant planned for lease-up season.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_the_.outcome: Planned staffing changes included in the payroll budget.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_the_.rootCause: Staffing plans change (adding a porter, a second leasing agent); the budget must include them.
scr_budgeting_adding_an_employee_to_the_.ifSkipped: Planned staffing additions are left out and payroll is under-budgeted.
redFlags: Additions without regional approval

scr_budgeting_viewing_an_employees_payro.purpose: Views one employee's calculated payroll budget — wages, overtime, taxes, benefits and workers' comp by month.
scr_budgeting_viewing_an_employees_payro.outcome: Line-level verification of an employee's budget.
scr_budgeting_viewing_an_employees_payro.rootCause: Spot-checking individual calculations confirms the payroll setup is producing correct results.
scr_budgeting_viewing_an_employees_payro.ifSkipped: Setup errors affecting all employees go undetected.
redFlags: Taxes continuing after wage bases are exceeded

scr_budgeting_management_fees_list.purpose: Lists management fee budget setups by property — fee percentage and fee base — used to calculate budgeted management fees from budgeted revenue.
scr_budgeting_management_fees_list.outcome: Management fees budgeted consistently with the management agreement.
scr_budgeting_management_fees_list.rootCause: Management fees are a percentage of revenue (often collections); budgeting them from budgeted revenue with the contract percentage keeps them consistent with the revenue plan.
scr_budgeting_management_fees_list.ifSkipped: Fee budgets are guessed and do not move with revenue changes.
redFlags: Fee percentage different from the agreement

scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.purpose: Calculates budgeted management fees from the working budget's revenue and the fee percentage.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.outcome: Fee budgets that follow revenue assumptions.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.rootCause: When revenue assumptions change during review, fees must be recalculated or the budget becomes internally inconsistent.
scr_budgeting_calculating_management_fee.ifSkipped: Fees do not reflect final revenue assumptions.
redFlags: Fees calculated on GPR when the agreement specifies collections

scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.purpose: Publishes the calculated management fee (fee percentage × budgeted fee base) into the management fee account of the property's working budget.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.outcome: The operating budget includes correctly calculated fees.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.rootCause: Publishing links the fee calculation to the budget so final numbers are consistent.
scr_budgeting_publishing_management_fees.ifSkipped: Budget fee lines stay stale after revenue assumptions change and the budget is internally inconsistent.
redFlags: Fees not republished after revenue changes

scr_budgeting_reports.purpose: Reports section of Forecasting & Planning — trial balance and GL reports for actuals, budget reports and stored or memorized reports.
scr_budgeting_reports.outcome: Budget and actuals reporting available from within planning.
scr_budgeting_reports.rootCause: Budget work needs actuals and budget reports side by side; having them in the planning area avoids switching applications.
scr_budgeting_reports.ifSkipped: Budget analysis relies on exports from other modules.
redFlags: Budget reports run on draft versions

scr_budgeting_my_stored_reports_list.purpose: Lists budget and actuals reports the user has stored — for example the final approved budget report sent to the owner — with generation dates.
scr_budgeting_my_stored_reports_list.outcome: A retained copy of the exact budget reports shared with owners.
scr_budgeting_my_stored_reports_list.rootCause: When a question arises months later about what the owner approved, the stored budget report shows exactly what was sent.
scr_budgeting_my_stored_reports_list.ifSkipped: The version of the budget shared with the owner cannot be reproduced.
redFlags: Approved budget report not stored

scr_budgeting_storing_standard_reports_a.purpose: Explains storing budget reports and charts — running them in the background and saving outputs for later use.
scr_budgeting_storing_standard_reports_a.outcome: Large budget reports run reliably and are retained.
scr_budgeting_storing_standard_reports_a.rootCause: Portfolio budget reports are large and time out when viewed live; storing them also preserves the approved version.
scr_budgeting_storing_standard_reports_a.ifSkipped: Large budget reports fail and approved versions are not retained.
redFlags: No stored copy of approved budgets

scr_budgeting_viewing_a_stored_report.purpose: Opens a stored budget or budget-vs-actual report once background generation completes, to review exactly the version that was produced for the owner.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_stored_report.outcome: Access to the saved budget output.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_stored_report.rootCause: Reviewing the stored version ensures discussions refer to exactly what was sent, not a regenerated report reflecting later edits.
scr_budgeting_viewing_a_stored_report.ifSkipped: Budget discussions use regenerated reports that differ from what was approved.
redFlags: Regenerated reports used in place of approved versions

scr_budgeting_choosing_file_types_to_sto.purpose: Chooses the file format for stored budget reports — PDF for owner approval packages, Excel for analysis.
scr_budgeting_choosing_file_types_to_sto.outcome: Budget reports stored in formats suited to their audience.
scr_budgeting_choosing_file_types_to_sto.rootCause: Owners approve budgets from fixed PDFs while accountants need Excel for analysis; storing both avoids rework.
scr_budgeting_choosing_file_types_to_sto.ifSkipped: Reports must be rerun in the needed format.
redFlags: Approval packages sent in editable formats

scr_budgeting_deleting_a_stored_report.purpose: Deletes stored budget reports that are no longer needed, since stored reports are kept until someone deletes them — while keeping the approved budget package.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_stored_report.rootCause: Unmanaged stored reports make the approved version hard to find, but deleting the approved version loses evidence.
scr_budgeting_deleting_a_stored_report.ifSkipped: Clutter; misuse deletes approved budget evidence.
redFlags: Deleting approved budget reports

scr_budgeting_storage_options_page.purpose: Chooses where a processed budget report is stored — My Stored Reports, cloud storage or the Reporting Portal.
scr_budgeting_storage_options_page.outcome: Budget reports delivered to the right audience's location.
scr_budgeting_storage_options_page.rootCause: Approved budgets are often published to owners through the Reporting Portal or shared cloud folders; storing directly avoids manual uploads.
scr_budgeting_storage_options_page.ifSkipped: Owners do not receive the approved budget through their expected channel.
redFlags: Draft budgets stored to owner-facing locations

scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_my_sto.purpose: Stores a processed budget report — for example the approved annual budget package — in the user's My Stored Reports so it can be reopened later exactly as sent.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_my_sto.outcome: A retained personal copy of the budget report.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_my_sto.rootCause: Preparers need the exact budget report they submitted for approval for later reference.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_my_sto.ifSkipped: The submitted version cannot be reproduced.
redFlags: Only personal copies, no shared evidence

scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_a_clou.purpose: Stores a budget report directly into a configured cloud storage location such as the owner's SharePoint budget folder.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_a_clou.outcome: Budget packages saved automatically where owners and teams expect them.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_a_clou.rootCause: Offshore teams deliver budget packages through shared folders; direct storage avoids missed or wrong-version uploads.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_a_clou.ifSkipped: Owner folders hold outdated budget versions.
redFlags: Cloud targets shared too broadly

scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_report.purpose: Stores a processed budget report in the RealPage Reporting Portal so owners and investors can access the approved budget through their portal login.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_report.outcome: Owners access approved budgets through the portal.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_report.rootCause: The portal is the owner-facing channel; publishing the approved budget there ensures owners see the official version.
scr_budgeting_storing_a_report_in_report.ifSkipped: Owners receive budgets through ad hoc emails with version risk.
redFlags: Drafts published to the portal

scr_budgeting_memorized_reports.purpose: Explains memorized budget reports — saved settings for budget and BVA reports that can be rerun or scheduled.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports.outcome: Budget reports produced consistently each cycle.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports.rootCause: Owners compare budget packages year to year; memorized settings keep formats consistent.
scr_budgeting_memorized_reports.ifSkipped: Budget packages vary in format and content year to year.
redFlags: Memorized reports pointing to prior-year budgets
